title: The Closest Exit
pageTitle: Understand Absolute Value of Rational Numbers
covers: absolute value as distance from zero for integers, fractions and decimals, and using it to compare how far things are from 0
cert: finding absolute value as distance from zero and using it to compare distances

intro.caption: Lesson 7-3 — absolute value. The Delvers made camp in the Tunnel of Echoes. One exit lies west, one lies east, and Kwame has just found a trapdoor. Three reader gates and a boss slime stand between the party and the rescue.

balloons.t: Camp is 0. West is negative, east is positive. The doors are at −6 and 4.
Kwame fell through a trapdoor into slime. Every stone he walks costs him a heart.
That's how I got here. Anyway! West door. −6 is smaller than 4, so it's CLOSER!
Smaller is not closer. Count the stones, Kwame.

pages.caption: −6 is less than 4. But "less" is about value, not distance. How FAR a number is from 0 is its absolute value, and distance is never negative.

balloons.t: Six stones west to that door. Distance doesn't care which way you walk.
Seven hearts. The east door costs 4 stones, so he keeps 3. The west door leaves him 1.
One heart is still a heart!
Compare distances, not signs. That's how we judge every claim.
Fine. Next time I'll also look before I step.
The Slime King only moves for right answers. Ready the rope!
Four stones, three hearts left. Best rescue ever.

win.caption: Absolute value is a number's distance from 0, so it is never negative: |−6| = 6 and |4| = 4. To find the closer place, compare absolute values, not the numbers themselves.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Distance from Zero
gates.prompt: Sol counts how far each spot is from camp at 0. That distance is the absolute value, written with bars: |−6|.
hints: Conceptual: absolute value is distance from 0. A distance is never negative, so the bars drop the direction.
Procedural: find the number on the line. Count the units back to 0. That count is the absolute value.

steps: −9 sits 9 units to the left of 0.

items.label: West door: |−6| =

fb.msg: Distance can't be negative. −6 is 6 stones from camp, so |−6| = 6.
0 would mean the door is AT camp. Count the stones from 0 to −6.

items.fbDefault: Count the units from −6 back to 0.

items.label: A puddle at −2¼: |−2¼| =
items.aria: absolute value of negative 2 and one quarter

fb.msg: Absolute value is a distance, so it is never negative. Drop the minus sign.
Keep the ¼. The puddle is 2¼ units from 0, not 2.
You kept only the fraction part. The whole distance is 2 and ¼.

items.fbDefault: −2¼ is between −3 and −2. How far is it from 0?

gates.pass: |−6| = 6 and |−2¼| = 2¼. Sol writes the distances on her map, all positive.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Which Door?
gates.prompt: Doors at −6 and 4. Fewer stones means more hearts for Kwame.
hints: Conceptual: a negative number is not closer just because it is less. Closer means a smaller distance from 0.
Procedural: find each absolute value. The smaller absolute value is the closer place.

steps: Practice: which is closer to 0, −2 or 5?

items.q: Which door is closer to camp?

options.fb: −6 IS less than 4, but less is not closer. |−6| = 6 stones and |4| = 4 stones.

options.t: East door, because |4| = 4 is less than |−6| = 6
Both doors are the same distance
options.fb: 6 stones and 4 stones are different distances. Only opposites like −4 and 4 are equally far.

items.q: A hidden door is just as far from camp as the east door, but on the west side. Mark it.

fb.msg: That's the east door itself. Go the same distance on the west side, left of 0.
That's camp. The hidden door is 4 stones from camp.
That's 5 stones west. The east door is only 4 stones away.

items.fbDefault: |4| = 4. Find the spot 4 units LEFT of 0.

gates.pass: East it is: 4 stones, not 6. The hidden door at −4 is just as close, but it's painted on the wall. Classic dungeon.

gates.title: Gate 3 · The Argument
gates.prompt: The Delvers argue about distances. Judge whose reasoning holds.
hints: Conceptual: to compare absolute values, compare distances from 0. Signs tell direction, not size.
Procedural: write each absolute value as a plain distance first. Then compare those two distances.

items.q: Kwame: "|−5| < |3| because −5 < 3." Anya: "|−5| > |3| because 5 > 3." Sol: "They are equal." Who is right?

options.fb: Kwame compared the numbers, not their distances. −5 is 5 units from 0, and 3 is only 3 units.
Equal would need the same distance. 5 units and 3 units are not the same.

items.q: Bao's chart: a trap took 8 hearts (−8). A potion gave back 5 (+5). Which change has the greater magnitude?

options.fb: +5 is the greater VALUE. Magnitude is size, the distance from 0: |−8| = 8 is bigger than 5.
8 hearts and 5 hearts are different sizes.

gates.pass: Anya wins the argument, and the trap's −8 was the bigger change. Kwame admits it. He also admits the trapdoor was clearly marked.

gates.title: Boss Gate · The Slime King
gates.prompt: The Slime King blocks the way. Three locks, then the rope goes out.
hints: Conceptual: for every lock, think distance from 0. Absolute value is never negative, and the sign only shows the side.
Procedural: write the absolute value of each number. Then order, compare or measure using those distances.

steps: Practice: which is farther from 0, −1.2 or 0.9?

items.q: Lock 1 · Which is farther from 0: −⅔ or ½?

options.fb: Being positive doesn't make it farther. |½| = ½ and |−⅔| = ⅔, and ⅔ > ½.
⅔ and ½ are different distances. Compare them: ⅔ is about 0.67.

items.q: Lock 2 · Tap the four doors from closest to camp to farthest.
items.fb: Order by distance from 0, not by value. |0.5| = 0.5, |−1.5| = 1.5, |3| = 3, |−4| = 4.

items.label: Lock 3 · The rope must reach a ledge at −3.5. Rope length in stones:
items.aria: rope length in stones to reach negative 3.5

fb.msg: A rope can't be −3.5 stones long. Length is distance: |−3.5| = 3.5.
Keep the half. The ledge is 3.5 stones from 0.

items.fbDefault: The rope's length is the distance from 0 to −3.5.

gates.pass: GLORP. The Slime King rolls aside. −⅔ is farther, the doors are in order, and 3.5 stones of rope fly through the door.

journal.heading: Lesson 7-3 — what the tunnel taught us
rows: How far a number is from 0. Written |−6|. It is never negative: |−6| = 6 and |6| = 6.
|−2¼| = 2¼ and |−3.5| = 3.5. Every rational number has a distance from 0.
−6 < 4, but |−6| = 6 is MORE than |4| = 4. The east door was closer.
The size of a change: a −8 trap has magnitude 8, bigger than a +5 potion.
A negative number is not closer just because it is less. Compare distances, not signs.
journal.quote: "Less is not closer. I learned that the slimy way." — Kwame

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 7-3 (Understand Absolute Value of Rational Numbers) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. It covers only this lesson: absolute value as distance from zero for integers, fractions and decimals, magnitude in context, and comparing distances from zero.
standards: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers
